items.text: That is the part that should actually drive your decision.
A quiz result or a single personality label will not settle this.

Content marketing wins on voice and independence: it rewards a genuine point of view that AI cannot convincingly fake once you have built it, the entry path does not depend on a specific degree, and it opens a well-worn road to ghostwriting, ongoing brand retainers, or a personal content brand once you have real results to show.

SEO wins on structure and provability: the skill is easier to self-test against a real website, the entry filter is more standardised and checklist-driven, and the technical range you build compounds into higher pay, especially now that AI-search optimisation is opening a new, higher-paying specialisation on top of classic SEO.
You think in stories, not just structures
You naturally notice the angle that makes a topic worth reading, not just the checklist that makes it rank.

blocks.heading: How to Start Learning Each for Free

items.text: Before you pay for a bootcamp or certification in either lane, test your fit on free material first.
Start a free personal blog or LinkedIn newsletter, pitch guest posts to small brands or startups, and study working writers whose style you admire.
This is the part most head-to-head comparisons skip entirely, and it is often the most useful answer for someone who genuinely likes parts of both fields.

SEO content strategy is not a vague hybrid title, it is a real, growing lane inside Indian D2C, SaaS, and media companies that specifically need someone who can write or brief content that a reader wants to finish and an algorithm wants to rank.

Plans content specifically to win search intent: chooses topics from keyword and competitor gap data, structures articles to satisfy both the reader and the algorithm, and tracks whether published pieces actually rank, not just whether they read well.

blocks.heading: Mistakes to Avoid When Making This Decision

items.text: Writing a personal caption and writing a brand narrative that a stakeholder will defend in a boardroom are not the same skill.
The checklist is learnable in a few months, which means the market has plenty of certificate-holders who have never fixed a real, messy website.

A portfolio of published pieces (even guest posts or a personal blog) that show a clear point of view, plus proof you can adapt tone across formats, a hiring manager wants to read your writing, not just your resume.

Comfort running a real audit on a real website: finding technical issues, prioritising them, and explaining the fix in plain language. Certificates matter less than a documented before-and-after case, even a small one.
